questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How farmers are changing the countryside
The best places for a country walk
Why fewer people go out into the countryside
How to take good photos in the countryside when the weather is bad
questions.why: Neil says the programme is about how fewer and fewer people are venturing out into the country.

questions.q: How does Catherine react when Neil asks about her last country walk?
options: She jokes that she didn't know people did that
She says she goes walking in the country every weekend
She says she much prefers walking around the city
She says she went yesterday
questions.why: She says 'People do that?' and 'people are strange.'

questions.q: Why does Catherine think the phrase 'venture out' might be part of the problem?
options: It is an old-fashioned phrase that nobody uses now
It makes going out sound risky
It is only used about the city
It sounds too relaxing
questions.why: She says 'venture out' suggests it's a big challenge, or even a risky activity.

questions.q: What did the survey find about millennials, according to Annabel Shackleton?
options: Most of them go to the countryside every week
They don't care about the countryside
They find the countryside boring
Many know it's good to go but still don't
questions.why: She says 4 in 10 think they should spend more time there, 'but they're just not going out'.

questions.q: How does Annabel Shackleton feel about the survey results?
options: Shocked and surprised
Pleased and proud
Bored
Not surprised at all
questions.why: Neil says she uses 'phenomenal' to show how shocked and surprised she is.

questions.q: Which excuse does Annabel Shackleton say people give for staying indoors?
options: The countryside is too far away
They are too busy at work
They don't have the right clothing
Walking is dangerous
questions.why: She says they use excuses like 'they haven't got the right clothing'.

questions.q: Why does Neil quote the saying about the wrong weather and the wrong clothing?
options: To agree that bad weather is a good excuse
To say weather shouldn't stop you if you dress well
To complain about the cold, wet British weather in the countryside
To advertise walking clothes
questions.why: He says 'there is no such thing as the wrong weather, just the wrong clothing!'

questions.q: According to Catherine, what could be a problem with going out in terrible weather?
options: You might get lost
The paths might be closed
You might catch a cold if you stay out in the rain for too long
Your photos might not be good enough for Instagram
questions.why: She says if the weather is terrible, you might not get good pictures for your Instagram account.
